causes.label: demand
causes.quote: The high temperature in the region resulted in a new summer demand record of 13 567 MW.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: The majority of this reduction was a result of unplanned outages and delays in returning generation plant to service.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: On 15 January, the Lower Tumut to Upper Tumut 64 line was out for service as part of a 12 day planned network outage that commenced on 5 January.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Over several rebids from 8.30 am, Delta Electricity shifted 540 MW of capacity across its portfolio, from prices below $100/MWh to above $9000/MWh.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Total import capability into New South Wales was around 290 MW lower than forecast four hours ahead.

interconnectors_named.name: Lower Tumut to Upper Tumut 64 line
interconnectors_named.quote: On 15 January, the Lower Tumut to Upper Tumut 64 line was out for service as part of a 12 day planned network outage that commenced on 5 January.

interconnectors_named.name: QNI
interconnectors_named.quote: The QNI import limit was close to forecast.

interconnectors_named.name: Terranora interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: Outages of equipment associated with the Terranora interconnector reduced import capability below nominal levels, further tightening the supply-demand balance in the region.

intervals.quote: On 15 January 2009, the spot market price in New South Wales exceeded $5000/MWh for the 2 pm trading interval.

network_outages.quote: On 15 January, the Lower Tumut to Upper Tumut 64 line was out for service as part of a 12 day planned network outage that commenced on 5 January.

peak_price.quote: On 15 January the spot price in New South Wales reached $5210/MWh at 2 pm.

rebid_set_price.quote: At the time around 1170 MW, or 9 per cent of available capacity in New South Wales was priced above $5000/MWh, 890 MW of which was from rebidding by participants.
